newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold demand upbeat after record figures.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold demand upbeat after record figures.

text.p: Dubai gold demand remained upbeat on Sunday, fanned by strong Indian wedding demand and buying ahead of a government-sponsored shopping festival in the Gulf emirate, traders based in Dubai said on Sunday.
Physical stock levels of the yellow metal in Dubai were said by traders to be low and price premiums to the international spot price rising despite record imports in January.
"Gold demand in Dubai is now pretty high...There is a shortage of physical gold in the market," said one trader.

The local market has been fired up because this year's plunge in international gold prices below the important $345-350 range coincided with a relaxtion in Indian import regulations and the Moslem holy fasting month of Ramadan.

"There is a lot more gold going to India because of the new policy of allowing 10 kg," one trader said, referring to new Indian laws that allow non-resident Indians to double the amount of gold they could bring into India every six months.
Falling prices, higher Indian demand and Ramadan caused a surge in gold imports in January to a record monthly high of 46.35 tonnes, the World Gold Council (WGC) in Dubai reported.
This represented a 92.6 percent increase over January 1996 import figures, WGC reported.
February was also seeing strong demand and high turnover because of the upcoming Indian wedding season and the Dubai Shopping Festival which starts at the end of March.
The 300-plus gold traders in Dubai use the festival to heavily promote jewellery and bullion retail business, offering numerous raffles and price discounts to increase turnover.
Dubai's Ten Tola bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24-carat gold -- was quoted by traders at 4,860-65 UAE dirhams ($1,323.52-24.89), up from 4,772 dirhams ($1,299.56) on February 16.
Premiums were also higher on limited stocks with TT premium commanding $1.50- $2.00 to the international price compared to a more typical $1.20-25, traders said.
Kilogram bar premiums were assessed at 80 cents to $1 compared to the usual 70 cents, traders said.
International bullion was last quoted on Saturday at $351.85-35 an ounce, above last week's 3-3/4 year low of $336.
